Package index

Fitting

The two models. They take the same data and the same formula, so a model can be refitted under the other by changing the function name alone.

pcdreg()
Semiparametric regression for panel count data

Specifying the data

The response constructor, used on the left hand side of the formula. See the data preparation article for the layouts it accepts.

pcd()
Describe panel count observations
is.pcd()
Test for a panel count response
autoplot(<pcd>) plot(<pcd>)
Plot panel count data

Inspecting a fit

Both fitters return an object inheriting from pcdfit, so these work the same way for either.

vcov(<pcdfit>)
Covariance matrix of the estimated coefficients
summary(<pcdfit>)
Summarise a fitted panel count model
baseline()
Estimated baseline function
predict(<pcdfit>)
Predictions from a panel count model
autoplot(<pcdfit>) plot(<pcdfit>)
Plot the estimated baseline function

Tidy output

Methods for the broom generics, so a fit drops into a tidy workflow: one row per coefficient, a one row summary of the fit, and the data with fitted means and residuals attached.

tidy(<pcdfit>) glance(<pcdfit>) augment(<pcdfit>)
Tidy a panel count model fit
reexports autoplot tidy glance augment
Objects exported from other packages

Tuning

pcdreg_control()
Tuning parameters for the fitting algorithms

Simulation

The design of the simulation study in Sun et al. (2024), useful for examples and for checking the covariance estimators against known truth.

sim_pcd()
Simulate panel count data with a time-varying covariate

Package

pcdreg-package
pcdreg: Semiparametric Regression for Panel Count Data
